page: Vultr vcg-a40-24c-120g-48vram is a dedicated instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The host is configured with 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 extensions. The platform includes 120.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Storage is provisioned via a 1400 GB local NVMe SSD, and the environment includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. While indexed within the Dedicated Metal GPU family, the reported hardware profile indicates zero active GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier execution across typical compute and system metrics. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 42692.67 and a single-core score of 1780.38, matching the PassMark CPU test score of 35837.28. Memory performance exhibits high throughput on uncached large-block read operations at 192.56 GB/sec, placing it in the upper 25 percent of tested systems. Application-level evaluations record 43.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 34.88 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound inference across medium language models registers 14.45 tokens per second for text generation, while larger models demonstrate steep performance degradation.

The hardware configuration offers a balanced resource ratio suited for medium-density data processing rather than accelerator-driven AI tasks. The combination of dedicated vCPUs, generous memory capacity, and 1400 GB of responsive local NVMe storage makes this configuration appropriate for backend database operations, caching tiers, compilation pipelines, container orchestration, and general-purpose enterprise application hosting.
